clue.text: Film of tea demonstrations preceding crazy rage

indicators.note: preceding tells us the protest pieces come first in the answer, with the angry pieces placed after them

blocks.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
violent street demonstrations
off, as in off one's head
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A documentary about tea-party protests that end in a fit of mad fury.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea, and 'off' can mean crazy, as in 'gone off his head'. The surface points at the American Tea Party, but the film is the 1981 Olympic running drama CHARIOTS OF FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariots of Fire is the Oscar-winning 1981 British movie about two runners at the Paris Olympics.

clue.text: Oh — rum stirred up the blood, for example

indicators.note: stirred up means agitated and mixed, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a drink of rum gets the blood pumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred up the blood' sounds like excitement; the blood is in fact an example of the answer. The spelling is American.
explanation.definitionFit: In old medicine blood was one of the four bodily humors, with phlegm and yellow and black bile.

clue.text: Step down is transposition for singer

indicators.note: a transposition swaps elements around, so the word's letters are given in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A musician moves to a lower note, a change of key for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step down' and 'transposition' both sound musical, a scale step and a key change; one is the definition, the other the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, which is what stepping down from a job means.

clue.text: Retrograde Delaware politician presents musical performance

indicators.note: presents means shows or displays, so the letters are on view inside the neighboring words
retrograde means moving backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A backward-looking congressman from Delaware puts on a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delaware politician' tempts you to look for a rep or senator, but the answer sits inside the words themselves: deLAWARE POlitician, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a form of musical performance.

clue.text: "Shaking the oyster" is a branch of mathematics

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the contents, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A quirky claim that shucking oysters counts as a mathematical discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Set theory is the field of mathematics that studies collections of objects and underlies much of modern mathematics.

clue.text: To a limited extent, zipper catches fashionable, ugly tie

indicators.note: catches means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
ugly suggests something misshapen, so the word that follows is rearranged

blocks.note: a fly is the zipper on a pair of trousers
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A zip partly snags on a trendy but unattractive necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a limited extent' reads like 'partly' introducing the snag; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Finitely means within bounds, in a way that has an end, so only to a limited degree.

clue.text: Brown and others with terribly vile fever taking many, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of that word is used
terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are thrown into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
an ague is a malarial fever with shivering
its final letter

explanation.surface: A man named Brown and companions catch a dreadful fever that kills many people.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a person's surname; it is Brown University in Rhode Island, one of the eight elite northeastern US colleges in this group.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown is one of the eight Ivy League universities, with Harvard, Yale and others, so the group is Brown and its peers.

clue.text: Tasteful hash of eel and gnat

indicators.note: a hash is a chopped-up mixture, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mock praise for a dish of chopped eel and insects as refined cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteful' sounds like it is about flavor, fitting the food; it means stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, showing good taste.

clue.text: Bombshell display in middle of street

indicators.note: in the middle of something means placed inside it, between its ends

blocks.note: an expo is an exhibition or public display
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A shocking show staged in the center of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombshell' suggests a shocking surprise; here it means a glamorous, very attractive person, as in blonde bombshell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a strikingly attractive woman, and a sexpot is slang for the same kind of sexually alluring person.

clue.text: Mothers, seen scattered outside in a crowd

indicators.note: letters that are scattered are thrown about and land in a new order
outside says the jumbled word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
ma is an informal word for mother, so mothers are mas

explanation.surface: Mothers are spotted spread out among a crowd of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen' reads as a verb describing the mothers, but it is the word that gets jumbled and wrapped around them.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is a French-derived phrase meaning all together as a group, which is what being in a crowd means.

clue.text: Vintage photo of a colorful gym class?

blocks.note: tinty means having a tint, so full of color
PE is physical education, the school gym class

explanation.surface: An old photograph of a brightly dressed school exercise class.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'a colorful gym class' is a whimsical way to split the answer, not a real description of the photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is a nineteenth-century photograph printed directly on a thin iron plate, so an antique picture.

clue.text: Norm Silver destroyed harp, gets consecutive sentences

indicators.note: something destroyed is smashed apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: par is the normal standard, as in golf
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Norm Silver smashes a harp and is jailed for several crimes in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm Silver' reads as a person's name and 'consecutive sentences' as prison terms; really they are PAR, AG and a run of written sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a block of writing made of sentences that follow one another.

clue.text: Time and heat disintegrated letter from Thucydides

indicators.note: something that has disintegrated has fallen to pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Time and heat have crumbled an ancient document written by Thucydides.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a crumbling manuscript; 'letter' is an alphabet letter, and Thucydides, a Greek historian, stands for the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a character of the Greek alphabet, which the Greek historian Thucydides wrote in.

clue.text: Military vehicle to fail completely

blocks.note: first meaning: an armored fighting vehicle on tracks
second meaning: a slang verb for collapsing or flopping badly

explanation.surface: An army vehicle that breaks down entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an armored combat vehicle, and as slang verb means to flop badly, as a film does at the box office.

clue.text: Reporter and actor capturing Southwestern ring

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner and holding within, so the other pieces go inside

blocks.note: Paul Newman, the American film actor
SW is the abbreviation for southwestern
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A journalist and a film star seize a gang operating in the Southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is Paul Newman, star of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A newswoman is a female journalist, someone who reports the news.

clue.text: Low luminescence, primarily found in darkness!

definitions.text: Low luminescence, primarily found in darkness

blocks.clueFragment: Low luminescence, primarily found in darkness
blocks.note: surface reading: a faint glow that you mostly see when it is dark
setter's reading: low is also the sound a cow makes, which starts the answer, and the rest is light seen at night

explanation.surface: A dim glow that shows up mostly once it gets dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works as one description of a gentle night-time light; 'Low' doubles as a cow's call, hinting at how the word begins. The clue gives no separate source for the fourth letter, so read it as a whole-clue definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The light reflected from the moon is soft and faint and is seen chiefly at night.

clue.text: Grievous violation viewed in a different way: "It's normal"

indicators.note: seeing something in a different way rearranges it, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a terrible offense, claiming it is perfectly ordinary from another perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a mortal sin is a grave wrong that cuts the soul off from grace, a serious moral transgression.

clue.text: Corrected trespass that's most widely scattered

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters are put into a different, proper order

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A trespass, once punished, becomes the most widespread offense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsest is the superlative of sparse, meaning thinly spread out over the widest area.

clue.text: Police ransacked pantry for outdoor festivity

indicators.note: a ransacked room is turned upside down, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the law is an informal name for the police
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Officers turn a pantry upside down looking for food for a garden celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn party is a social gathering held on a garden lawn, an open-air celebration.

clue.text: Appear to sing "New York's Getting Higher" in amateurish clip

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting higher means rising up the column, so the letters read from bottom to top
in places one piece inside the other
something amateurish is clumsily put together, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
NY is New York, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A singer mimes a song called 'New York's Getting Higher' in a homemade video.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-sync is to mouth the words of a recording so that it looks as if you are really singing.

clue.text: Small, soft cry

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and British for small
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A tiny, quiet whimper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small, soft cry' reads as one description of a sound; it splits as two pieces plus the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, a synonym for the verb cry.

clue.text: Lead around unsavory fare that's ready-made

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes on either side of the second
unsavory suggests something unpleasant or messed up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone guides others past nasty convenience food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb meaning guide; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefab is short for prefabricated, describing something built in advance and ready to assemble.

clue.text: Turkey beside slice of onion and fruit, surprisingly

indicators.note: a slice is only a small part, so just the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a tom is a male turkey
at means beside, as in at the door
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cookery note: turkey served with sliced onion and, unexpectedly, fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition: botanically this salad staple counts as a fruit, which many people find surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is botanically a fruit, a seed-bearing berry, though it is usually cooked and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Initially, planets (or worlds) emitting radiation might…

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: its opening letter
its opening letter
its opening letter
its opening letter
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Planets or worlds giving off radiation might do something, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb finishing the sentence; it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun means strength or force, the same as power.

clue.text: …scramble iPod: Earth and Venus, essentially

indicators.note: to scramble is to mix up, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, radiation from the planets might scramble an iPod, and Earth and Venus are mentioned as examples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venus, essentially' looks like the planet's core; 'essentially' means 'in essence', and in essence Venus is the Greek goddess under a Roman name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love whom the Romans called Venus, so she is the same deity in essence.

clue.text: Capital of Hawaii maintaining answer: no

indicators.note: maintaining means holding or keeping, so the other pieces sit inside

blocks.note: HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii
A is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz: is Hawaii's capital the answer? No.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Hawaii' tempts you towards Honolulu; 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Very tired after exchanging words and accounting for everything

indicators.note: exchanging the words swaps the two halves of the phrase, the back part moving to the front

blocks.note: all in is an informal phrase for exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted after trading words and doing all the bookkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means in total, counting everything together, as in 'ten dollars in all'.

clue.text: Talks incessantly with people harvesting sweet potatoes?

blocks.note: first meaning: chatters on and on
second meaning, whimsical: those who gather yams, read as yam-ers

explanation.surface: Someone chatters nonstop alongside workers digging up sweet potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: in American usage a yam is a sweet potato, so people picking them are yam-mers.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to talk loudly and at length; split as yam plus -mers it becomes yam-harvesters.

clue.text: Falls, returning to win a race halfway

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left
halfway means only the first half of the word is kept and the rest is dropped

blocks.note: to gain is to win, then read backwards
taken as written
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: A runner falls over, going back to win a race after being only halfway round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb about tripping; it is the noun, the waterfall on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the border of New York State and Ontario, known simply as the Falls.

clue.text: City takes in sun-baked metal pole in disrepair

indicators.note: something in disrepair is broken down, so the letters are reassembled out of order

blocks.note: to take someone in is to con them
skin baked by the sun turns tan
tin is a metal
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A city's council accepts a rusting, sunbaked metal pole that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes in' looks like a container signal, but here it means deceives.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantinople was the historic name of the city on the Bosphorus now called Istanbul.
